Meticulous

/muh-TIK-yuh-lus/ — stress on TIK · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone who is meticulous is extremely careful and pays close attention to every small detail in their work.

The meticulous jeweler checked every link of the chain twice.

Worked Example

The meticulous surgeon reviewed the X-rays three times, checking every bone before making any cut.

Meticulous captures not just carefulness but obsessive attention to every tiny detail. 'Careful' alone misses the sense of systematic checking and fear of error that defines meticulous work.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

careful: giving steady attention to avoid mistakes

precise: exact and accurate in every small measurement

thorough: complete, leaving no step unchecked or unfinished

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

careless: paying too little attention, causing avoidable mistakes

slapdash: done hurriedly with no care for detail

Where it sits · how closely every detail gets checked — careless → hasty → careful → meticulous

careless vs. meticulous: Careless sits at the very bottom of the scale from meticulous: a careless worker skips details entirely, while a meticulous one examines every single detail.

hasty vs. meticulous: Hasty is far below meticulous: a hasty person rushes and overlooks small things, the exact opposite of the meticulous habit of double-checking everything.

careful vs. meticulous: Careful is on the way to meticulous but weaker: a careful student avoids obvious errors, while a meticulous one verifies every tiny detail twice.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — metic

Root — metic: fear, dread (from Latin metus, 'fear,' as it appears in meticulosus, 'fearful')

Suffix — -ulous

Suffix — -ulous: full of, characterized by (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Metic ('fear, dread,' from Latin metus, 'fear') + -ulous ('full of') — meticulous is literally 'full of fear.' It once meant timid; today it describes someone so afraid of making even a tiny mistake that they check every detail with extreme care.

Use the root in a new word: cautious

Use the root in a new word: cautious: A cautious driver is 'full of caution,' built with the same -ous ending that makes meticulous mean 'full of (almost fearful) care' about every detail.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / professional

Meticulous is the word for work that is almost obsessive — painstaking, detail-obsessed, and driven by a fear of making even tiny mistakes. Reach for it when the precision is extreme and slow. For everyday carefulness, 'careful' is simpler and more natural.
